dialogue.speaker: metal-inspector
dialogue.text: The transfer note says the triangle pointed the other way at the hall. The buyer thinks the desk issued a fresh tag. An apprentice remembers turning the tag to read its back. Use the blue practice tag to try each explanation. Reset the stand before each run.

options.text: Turn the practice tag on its cord.
Keep the stand still and hang a fresh tag.

dialogue.speaker: metal-inspector
dialogue.text: The cut triangle now points the other way. The nick beside the old hole is still there when you run a finger over it. The stand and cord stayed fixed.

options.text: Reset the stand for another run.

dialogue.speaker: metal-inspector
dialogue.text: The fresh blue tag also makes the triangle point the other way. Its hole has a clean edge. The stand and cord stayed fixed. The transfer note gives the direction and colour. It leaves both explanations open.

options.text: Reset the stand for another run.

dialogue.speaker: metal-steward
dialogue.text: We can check the two workshop keys and both bench runs now. Each shop uses a triangle at a different step. The reversed mark gives us two explanations to keep open. Attach the two shop keys and both results where readers can check them.

options.text: Hang the explanation at the yard handover.
File the explanation by the Trade Hall index.

dialogue.speaker: metal-steward
dialogue.text: Corra leaves two tags on hooks by the handover. One reader turns the old tag and another tries the fresh one. The separate shop keys stay at eye level. A buyer across the hall can ask a yard worker to show the difference.

dialogue.speaker: metal-steward
dialogue.text: Bea slips the run notes beside the index. A reader follows “fit checked” back to the fitting shop and “surface to check” to the coating bench. The transfer note keeps its own line. The reader can ask the yard for a hands-on run.

dialogue.speaker: metal-inspector
dialogue.text: Six sleeves came off the practice pieces. The yard needs clean ones back this shift. An apprentice went all the way to the hall for stock that was still here. Mark all six slots on one strip before copying either return count.

options.text: Clip Leila’s folded witness strip to the tally.
Clip the yard’s spare strip to the tally.
Leave the empty tally by the sleeves.

dialogue.speaker: metal-inspector
dialogue.text: The fold held a guide’s starting corner in the Nile Archive. It can keep the same six slots in order here. Check the clean stand in the yard and the repair tray across the hall.

dialogue.speaker: metal-inspector
dialogue.text: The fold keeps six spaces in order as the tally moves. Check the clean stand in the yard and the repair tray in the trade hall.

dialogue.speaker: metal-steward
dialogue.text: The four clean sleeves and two torn ones fill the same six slots. There is a place for the next yard run and a place for the repairs. Keep the clean stock in the yard for a quick start and send only the repair tray. Or move all six together so we can check them on one hall bench. The clean ones will wait here for the next cart.

options.text: Keep four clean sleeves at the yard and send two for repair.
Send the six together to the shared sorting stand.
Leave the two counts open for the next shift.

dialogue.speaker: metal-steward
dialogue.text: The yard takes the four straight back to the packing stand. We leave a repair tray for the other two and a duplicate line so the next shift can reconcile them. Check each end before the cart goes.

dialogue.speaker: metal-steward
dialogue.text: The carrier loads one tray. At the hall I split it between clean stock and repairs. The next yard run waits for a return cart, but I can check the whole count from one stand.

missions.title: The Turned Tag
missions.knowledgeQuestion: How can two explanations fit one observation, and what would separate them?

objectives.title: Try two ways the tag could change, then check the trip note and both shop keys.
Put both runs and the shop keys where people can check them.

missions.title: The Sleeves That Come Back
missions.knowledgeQuestion: How can a return count change what a workshop keeps in use?

objectives.title: Trace the six returned sleeves between yard and hall.
Choose a return route and check where its sleeves are held.

hints.text: The reversed triangle has at least two possible explanations.
Use the practice tag stand in the yard. The original box slips can stay in the hall.
Try a turn and a replacement on the same stand. The two shop keys and the old trip note show what you can carry back from the trial.
Handle the tag both ways. Read the fitting key by the yard table and the coating key by the Trade Hall window. The older trip note lies below the hall desk.
The two workshop keys and the runs are ready to travel together.
Go to Bea’s explanation clips in the Trade Hall.
Keep the two ways a tag could move beside both shop rules.
Choose a place where readers can check the explanation: the yard handover or the hall index.
Two workshops can move the same stock and make two entries for it.
Clip a strip to the return tally at the Sample Yard.
Check the clean sleeves in the yard and the repair tray in the Trade Hall.
Give each physical sleeve its slot in the same six. The cart is a journey for the sleeves.
The clean stock can return immediately or wait for the hall cart.
Find Bea’s return board beside the repair tray.
Choose whether to fill both local stands or sort the whole return in the hall.
Read both trays if you split the batch, or see both counts at the single hall stand.

moments.did: You tried two explanations on one stand and kept the shop records with your results.
moments.prompt: What trace would help you choose between the two explanations?

chronicle.title: The turned tag
chronicle.text: A turned tag and a fresh tag could both reverse the triangle. The shop keys travel with the two trial notes.

journal.text: The strip kept the yard and hall in one count. Four sleeves could go back into use. Two needed repair. We chose where the next shift could find them.
